claim: Studies that have looked at the effect of school closures on the overall rate of SARS-CoV-2 transmission find mixed results.

claim: Cases were assigned to clusters based on being at the same school and being reported within 7 days of each other.
source: We then assigned cases to clusters based on being at the same school and being reported within 7 days of each other; if the difference in date between two cases was less than or equal to 7 days, or they could be linked by a sequence of such cases, they were put in the same cluster.
evidence: Describes the methodology used in the study

claim: The choice of 7 days for cluster assignment was based on estimates of the serial interval for COVID-19 of approximately 5 days.

source: According to our model with parameters estimated from the data, in all four provinces (i) more than 65% of non-index cases occur in the 20% largest clusters
evidence: Calculated from the model with estimated parameters

claim: Reducing instantaneous transmission rate is effective in reducing the total number of cases.
source: According to our model with parameters estimated from the data, in all four provinces (i) more than 65% of non-index cases occur in the 20% largest clusters, and (ii) reducing instantaneous transmission rate and the number of contacts a student has at any given time are effective in reducing the total number of cases, whereas strict bubbling (keeping contacts consistent over time) does not contribute much to reduce cluster sizes.

claim: Reducing the number of contacts a student has at any given time is effective in reducing the total number of cases.
